rationale: The hypothesis posits that missense variants in the CxxC zinc finger domain of KDM2B have >75% penetrance for severe structural eye anomalies (coloboma, microphthalmia, anophthalmia). However, clinical series of patients with CxxC domain variants explicitly contradict this high penetrance rate. Specifically, Gomes et al. (2026) report three consecutive individuals with KDM2B CxxC domain variants who all exhibited non-structural refractive errors (myopic astigmatism) rather than severe structural anomalies (0/3, 0%). Furthermore, while Ceroni et al. (2026) identified two cases with structural eye defects, this cohort was ascertained by intentionally screening 706 families already presenting with developmental eye disorders, introducing strong ascertainment bias. In broader cohorts of CxxC domain variants (van Oirsouw et al., 2025; Gomes et al., 2026), ophthalmological anomalies are common, but severe structural malformations do not approach >75% penetrance.

evidence.text: In a targeted case series of three pediatric patients with heterozygous variants in the CxxC domain of KDM2B confirmed by epigenetic signature analysis, all three presented with myopic astigmatism, and none had severe structural ocular defects such as coloboma, microphthalmia, or anophthalmia.

source.title: KDM2B‐Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder A Case‐Series Supporting the CxxC Domain Phenotype With Emphasis on Ocular and Dermatologic Features
source.journal: American Journal of Medical Genetics Part A
source.quote: Patient 1 is a 2-year-old boy with developmental delay, solitary kidney, atrial septal defect, feeding difficulties, hemangiomas, and myopic astigmatism. Patient 2 is a 2-year-old girl with global developmental delay, hip dysplasia, feeding difficulties, hemangiomas, and myopic astigmatism. Patient 3 is a 5-year-old girl with autism, developmental delay, atrial septal defect, and ventricular septal defect, hypertrichosis, atopic dermatitis, and myopic astigmatism.

numbers.metric: Patients with severe structural eye anomalies (coloboma/microphthalmia/anophthalmia)

evidence.text: Screening of 706 families with developmental eye disorders identified two individuals with KDM2B CxxC domain missense variants (p.Arg614Pro and p.Cys627Ser) displaying complex structural eye defects, demonstrating that structural anomalies can occur but within an ascertainment cohort selected specifically for developmental eye defects.

source.title: Variants in the CxxC domain of the epigenetic regulator KDM2B support its role in developmental eye anomalies
source.quote: By screening 706 families with developmental eye disorders, we identified two cases with KDM2B-CxxC variants, NM_032590.5:c.1841G>C;p.(Arg614Pro) and NM_032590.5:c.1880G>C;p.(Cys627Ser), both resulting in a characteristic KDM2B DNA episignature. Both individuals exhibited complex structural eye defects, with neurodevelopmental, cardiac and renal anomalies variably present.

numbers.metric: Families with developmental eye disorders screened

evidence.text: In a systematic cohort of 19 individuals with KDM2B CxxC variants, congenital heart defects were the predominant malformation (present in up to 78%), while ophthalmological anomalies were described as common alongside musculoskeletal and urogenital anomalies, without establishing a >75% penetrance of severe structural eye defects.

source.title: KDM2B variants in the CxxC domain impair its DNA-binding ability and cause a distinct neurodevelopmental syndrome
source.quote: Congenital heart defects were observed in up to 78% of individuals, with additional common findings including musculoskeletal, ophthalmological, and urogenital anomalies, as well as behavioral challenges and feeding difficulties.

numbers.metric: Total individuals analyzed with CxxC variants

conflicts: Ascertainment in eye malformation cohorts (Ceroni et al., 2026) identified complex structural eye anomalies in 2/2 KDM2B-CxxC patients, whereas general neurodevelopmental cohorts (Gomes et al., 2026) report 0/3 individuals having structural eye defects, presenting instead with refractive errors like myopic astigmatism.

new_directions.question_text: What is the true unbiased penetrance of structural ocular anomalies versus refractive errors across all known individuals with KDM2B CxxC missense variants?
new_directions.rationale: Current cohorts differ drastically by ascertainment criteria (ophthalmic vs neurodevelopmental clinics), obscuring true penetrance.

new_directions.question_text: Do specific residues within the CxxC domain (e.g., zinc-coordinating cysteines vs basic DNA-contact residues) differentially affect ocular organogenesis pathways?
new_directions.rationale: Differences in residual DNA binding or PRC1.1 recruitment between missense variants may explain why some patients develop coloboma/microphthalmia while others develop only refractive errors.
